title: Pan pipes
reference_instrument: an Andean siku, for family likeness and with no count: the nearest isolated tube by pitch from the Wikimedia Commons set Registro sonoro del Siku (D3 from Bajo Sanja - Arca, G3 and D4 from Sanja - Ira, B4 from Contra Suli - Arca; Abel Christian Apaza Amanqui, Sikuri Sumaq Taqi, CC BY-SA 4.0). A siku is a different instrument from the modelled stopped pipes and is not tuned to A440
summary: Nothing here is graded: no licensed pan-pipe recording is in the library, and the clip beside each note is a real siku tube picked by pitch, not the pipe modelled. A twelfth sounds along with each note, even harmonics are far too weak, and the tubes come from published rules, not measurements. Each stopped tube takes its length from its note, its bore from Fletcher's scaling of measured panpipes and its lip-jet controls from flute players' relations, blown one tube at a time. The jet is a forced Bickley jet with momentum drive, Fletcher's 1976 spreading as a trial, a swing limit, a labium offset of half its half-width, and breath noise. About 10 dB of the strong third harmonic sits in the step from the cut flow to the mouth, and we don't know which loss is missing. D3's fundamental takes about 350 ms to arrive.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a lip jet on one stopped tube at a time, with the blowing pressure and jet length at each pitch from Fletcher 1975's flute-player relations, by analogy, as Fletcher 2005 does for jet speed
The stopped pipe, closed at the far end and open at the blown top, with the tube's length computed from its note and the bore from Fletcher 2005's scaling of European panpipes
A forced Bickley jet deflected by the window's own acoustic flow, leaving the flue with a Kutta condition
The jet's momentum drive (Thwaites and Fletcher 1983, Eq. 1, as printed). Without it D3, G3 and D4 sound their third mode, a twelfth above the named note
Jet spreading by Fletcher 1976, a trial here: it was measured on flues of 0.25 to 1.0 mm, and these run from 2.00 mm at D3 to 1.00 mm at B4
A labium offset of half the jet's half-width where it meets the lip (Fletcher 2005, Eq. 6): 1.09, 0.96, 0.80 and 0.62 mm at D3, G3, D4 and B4
A limit on how far the jet can swing: Fletcher 1976's envelope, with no coefficient to set. The way it's applied in time is ours
Contraction loss at the flue exit (Auvray et al. 2014, Table I), carried from the recorder's mouth to a stopped pipe

Breath noise at the window edge (Verge 1995, p. 196): gain 1.3e-3 of the jet's dynamic pressure, from a flue Reynolds number of 700, through an order-two Butterworth band-pass, carried to these flues as an extrapolation
Computed baffled radiation with a compact baffled reaction at the mouth, and Stokes-Kirchhoff air along the path to a receiver 1 m above the open top
The gas Coltman 1968 measured in a played flute's bore, applied to a stopped pipe by analogy, with dry air at 20 C outside
physics_missing: A graded comparison: each page sets its note beside one bamboo siku tube, the nearest by pitch among 94 recorded, with no count. A siku is a different instrument and isn't tuned to A440, and the tubes vary widely
A measured instrument: no siku or zampona tube lengths or bores are on the card, so this is a design from published rules

A weaker third harmonic: H3 reads -7.2, -6.3, -5.5 and -5.1 dB re H1 at D3, G3, D4 and B4, where the printed spectra put it at -12 dB near 390 Hz and -28 dB near 760 Hz. Taken apart from the render, about 10 dB of that sits in the step from the cut flow to the flow at the mouth. Neither the jet nor the pipe's resonance height is the cause. One suspect, from reading only: Fletcher describes energy lost to mixing just outside the mouth, and the engine's mouth has no such term

Even harmonics: H2 reads -60.6, -60.0, -59.2 and -58.0 dB at D3, G3, D4 and B4. A stopped pipe takes the second harmonic down 47 to 52 dB on its way to the mouth. Fletcher's two printed notes have about -51 and -28 dB, and the 94 recorded tubes a median of -17.0 dB

A printed jet speed on the low notes: D3 runs at 14.1 m/s and G3 at 16.3 m/s, under Fletcher's stated range of about 20 to 40 m/s. At 20 m/s with the jet length unchanged, on the card before the swing limit, they play the third mode even with the momentum drive. We tried no other jet length
Prompt speech on the low tubes: D3's fundamental takes about 350 ms to arrive, with the tube's third mode level with it until about 0.25 s
Pitch: the notes read -1.9, -3.1, -6.3 and -11.1 c from equal temperament at D3, G3, D4 and B4. Nothing was aimed at this
Neighbouring tubes aren't coupled, and the array's radiation and the player's lips and face aren't there
The percussive Andean playing style with a turbulent jet. The onset ramp is authored, not a player's
A closed end with no outlet: the input needs a radiating outlet, so a tiny vent stands in for it
